doc: SPORE design tokens — Neo-Tokyo Tactical Wasteland. See docs/VISUALDESIGN.md §1.
note: The one place a colour is defined. docs/VISUALDESIGN.md stays normative for the *reasoning*; this file is normative for the *values*, and design/generate.py emits them into site/style.css, web/build-standalone.mjs, android Chrome.kt and VISUALDESIGN's contrast table. Contrast ratios are computed from these hexes, never typed. Changing a value here and regenerating is the whole workflow; CI fails if the tree is stale.

palette.label: CRT Black
palette.role: page base, the dark of a powered-down screen

palette.label: Deep Moss
palette.role: crate fills, inert chrome, disabled states — olive drab that something has grown on

palette.label: Radioactive Pink
palette.role: the kawaii accent, cursor, primary action

palette.label: Copper Oxide
palette.role: hardware and wear — hinges, screws, rubbed edges. The warm mid-tone the palette lacked

semantic.role: borders — olive shifted dark, reads as machined metal
headings, UI chrome, code, LEDs, badges — short text
long-form body copy (site only) — amber at ~60% saturation
failure — pink does double duty; rely on the icon too

light.doc: Field Notes — the printed-manual voice, not a wash of the dark one. Every accent darkened to hold 4.5:1 on paper.

semantic.role: aliases to ink — dark ink on cream is already the comfortable read

fonts.stack: ui-monospace, "Cascadia Mono", "Fira Code", Menlo, Consolas, monospace
Impact, Haettenschweiler, "Arial Narrow Bold", system-ui, sans-serif
fonts.note: No webfont: the standalone node must make zero network requests, and CI asserts it. A display face is a system stack or it is nothing.

contrast.note: Grades are asserted both ways: a pair declared readable must compute readable, and a pair declared forbidden must compute forbidden. Either kind of stale claim fails the build.

extra.note: de-emphasised text still has to be readable

prose_notes:
**Never put pink on the moss.** {pink_on_moss}:1 is unreadable, and it is the one combination
the palette invites — hot pink stickers on an ammo crate. Put the sticker on a
`--void` or `--asphalt` patch instead, or outline it. The 2026-08-02 refinement
made this *more* forbidden, not less: it was 2.32:1 against Kevlar Olive.
Amber on the moss is large-text only ({amber_on_moss}:1): headings and buttons, never body copy.

Copper is hardware, not text. It reads on `--void` and, for large text only, on `--asphalt` — and it is forbidden on the moss ({copper_on_moss}:1), which is exactly where a hinge would sit. Draw wear with it; do not label with it.
contrast.prose_notes_doc: Authored prose, computed numbers. The wording is human — 'olive' reads better than the token name — but every ratio in it is substituted from the hexes, so the sentences cannot outlive the palette they describe.

metrics.doc: Sizing, spacing and shape — the C5 control system. Colour was single-sourced first (C3); these are the other half of the same argument, and their absence is why button heights, paddings and radii drifted apart across screens.
metrics.note: Every value here is one already in the tree, lifted rather than invented, so adopting the tokens renders identically. `chip` and `row` are the two exceptions: they name controls that did not exist yet (C5's Chip, C6's ListRow).
metrics.units: dp on Android, px on the web. The two agree by construction at 1x.

controls.role: primary and secondary buttons, and text fields — one height for all three
compact presets and toggles (7D/14D/30D, topics). NEW — must still carry a 48dp touch target
list rows for the Bridges/Advanced restructure (C6). NEW

shape.role: corner radius, everywhere — CrateShape already used it
the pressed-button offset and its drop shadow

touch.role: WCAG/Material floor. `control` and `row` clear it by height; `chip` must be padded out to it.

site.note: The docs site. Carries --prose because doc pages are read start-to-finish for minutes at a stretch.

standalone.note: One self-contained file, so it inlines resolved hexes rather than a raw-plus-semantic indirection. Its longest text is the one .tag paragraph, so no --prose.

android.note: Compose reads raw colours and maps them in SporeDarkColors/SporeLightColors, so the generated object is the palette only. Body text is chat bubbles and status rows, never a long read, so full amber stays and there is no --prose equivalent.
